mtp_finding.verdict: named capability gap: the model carries no MTP/NextN head, so no speculative route applies to Gemma 4. The gap is the model's, not a gate the engine imposes.
mtp_finding.engine_route: the in-tree speculative path is a NextN head: it reads tensors named nextn.enorm and nextn.hnorm (hipengine/runtime/qwen35_gguf_nextn.py, qwen4_exp_mtp.py). Presence of those tensors is what the route keys on, so an artifact that carried a NextN head is what the existing path reads; nothing in the engine refuses a Gemma 4 MTP head by model name.
mtp_finding.declaration: Gemma4GGUFGenerator.supports_speculative_mtp is already False (hipengine/generation/gemma4_gguf.py) and is surfaced through engine_service.supports_speculative_mtp, so the server already reports the capability as absent. This finding confirms the declaration against the artifact rather than changing it.
mtp_finding.consequence: decode cannot be accelerated by speculative decoding on this model, so decode work has to come from the single-token path: attention and the projection routes.

decode_lever_closed.candidate: raise the decode attention kernel's barrier batch. The 2026-09-24 decode specialization batches barrier rounds across 8 keys and halved the reduction barrier cost, so a larger batch is the obvious next step.
decode_lever_closed.measured: the batch is not a tunable. gemma4_attention.hip derives it per launch as the largest candidate from 8, 4, 2, 1 whose partial rows fit the 64 KB LDS budget, and the switch already carries a case 16 that the search never selects. It is therefore already at the hardware budget maximum on this target, and raising it needs a different reduction layout rather than a larger constant.
decode_lever_closed.verdict: closed by reading the selection rule against the hardware limit

decode_state.improvement: 1.31x over the gfx1151 baseline, public-path token-id parity exact
decode_state.source: recorded campaign rows: the 2026-09-24 bit-exact decode attention specialization (16.09 -> 20.48 tok/s) plus the later accepted units (-> 21.06 tok/s at 1024 prompt / 128 output). No decode throughput was added by this unit.
decode_state.where_the_time_goes: decode is device-bound. At KV~4096 attention is 79.2% of decode device time; at KV~129 it is 24%, with q4_k 23% and pack8 19% over 410 launches per step. The campaign's decode row is at 1024 prompt / 128 output, between those two.

remaining_levers_and_why_they_are_blocke.attention split: rejected at the numerical gate (kl_max 0.304 against 0.05, attributed to bf16-KV amplification), so it is changed arithmetic rather than an open optimization.
remaining_levers_and_why_they_are_blocke.q4_k decode re-route: blocked on a missing Q5_1 compact down kernel (no table entry in any family) and an expert_ffn % 256 guard the artifact's ffn=704 fails.
remaining_levers_and_why_they_are_blocke.pack8 dense decode rewrite: rejected: not bit-exact, and the measured mechanism is pinned by tests/test_gpu_gguf_q8_0_pack8_gemv_decode_parity.py.
remaining_levers_and_why_they_are_blocke.pack8 launch count: 410 launches per step is a real cost but the route is already selected; cutting the count means graph capture or a batched dense GEMV, and the campaign records graph capture as following stable pointer and state ownership rather than preceding it.

fresh_public_row.why: the decode figure cited above is the recorded campaign measurement. This re-measures it on the current tree through the same public runner, so that the acceptance's public-path parity claim is not resting on a number taken before this session's prefill units.
fresh_public_row.command: run_instrumented from scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py, 1024 prompt / 128 output, one warm repeat and three timed repeats, capacity 8192
fresh_public_row.observation: decode measures 20.03 against the recorded 21.06, about 5% lower, while prefill in the same process is within 1% of its own earlier measurement (6.021 s against 5.963 s at 1024 tokens). This is recorded as an unresolved observation, not explained away. The attribution evidence available is that the only kernel change this session made outside the prefill projection routes is the prefill attention reduction, which is a different kernel from the decode one and whose own A/B recorded decode unchanged at 21.048 against 21.063. Decode is the more launch-sensitive of the two phases, so a host difference would show there first, but no A/B across this session's commits was run to settle it.
fresh_public_row.next_check: re-run this row on a stashed tree at the commit that recorded 21.06 to separate a host effect from a regression.
